newsitem.title: INDIA: India NALCO sees lower aluminium exports.
newsitem.headline: India NALCO sees lower aluminium exports.

text.p: India's state-run National Aluminium Co (NALCO) said on Monday that it expects its aluminium exports to fall to 55,000 tonnes in 1997/98 (April-March) from 65,000 in 1996/97.
"I think our exports will be about 55,000 tonnes this year," NALCO chairman S.N. Johri told Reuters by telephone from the eastern city of Bhubaneshwar.
Johri said that in 1996/97, London Metal Exchange (LME) prices were depressed, spurring Indian imports of aluminium to meet domestic demand.
"But this year, LME prices are higher," Johri said. "Therefore imports (by India) will be less. Hence, the domestic demand has to be met by domestic supplies."
That would reduce the availability for export, he added.
Traders in Singapore said last week that the volume of aluminium shipments from NALCO had dipped to about 300 tonnes per week compared with a normal average of 500 to 800.
"I think exports this month will be the same as last month," Johri said. NALCO exported 4,653 tonnes of aluminium in May.
Johri did not give weekly export figures.
NALCO, Asia'a largest aluminium maker, produced 203,650 tonnes of aluminium in 1996/97 compared with 192,288 tonnes in 1995/96.
It produced a total of 33,851 tonnes of aluminium in April and May compared with 34,725 in the same two-month period in 1996.
